miguel: hey team — I'm prepping a residency matrix for MENA + LATAM. I opened a small docs PR with an SDK snippet and some migration notes for customers moving from global to regional endpoints: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/2345. The snippet currently uses `client.setRegion('me-south-1')` and shows a header `X-Redwood-Region: me-south-1`. Can someone weigh in on the legal phrasing we should use for 'data residency' across Hosted / Dedicated / Private, and whether the SDK example should prefer an env var vs method call? pinging @claire @ira @sam — cc @docs-bot

claire: looking now. can we prefer env var examples? that's the pattern our SDKs ship with (REDWOOD_REGION). also suggest we add one line about latency vs residency tradeoff so customers understand why they'd pick a region. i'll paste a suggested snippet in a sec.

claire: suggested snippet:
```
# example (node):
process.env.REDWOOD_REGION = 'me-south-1'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: process.env.REDWOOD_REGION })
const res = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hello' })
```
Also add a one-sentence note: "Selecting a nearby region reduces latency; selecting a region for residency may change the default fallback behavior."

sam: quick legal note from my side — we should avoid saying "guaranteed in-region storage" for Dedicated unless there's an explicit contract addendum. For Hosted we can say "data is processed and stored in the selected region where available" but prefer "processing locations" wording. Ira, can you confirm the safer phrasing?

ira: agree with sam. Recommended phrasing to use in docs: "For Hosted plans, customer content is processed and stored in the selected region where available. For Dedicated and Private deployments, physical control and contractual residency can be arranged via your agreement (see our Data Processing Addendum)." Please link the DPA: https://redwood.example.com/dpa. Also add a short footnote clarifying logs and backups: "Some operational metadata (e.g., global telemetry used for platform health) may be processed outside the selected region; see DPA for details."

miguel: thanks — i've updated the PR with that language and replaced the setRegion example with the env var snippet. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/2345/files. I also added a migration note under "Regional endpoints" that shows the curl change (global -> region subdomain). Example curl I added:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-Redwood-Region: me-south-1" https://api.me-south-1.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

docs-bot: Docs CI: ✅ 2/2 checks passed (links, lint). Preview: https://deploy-preview.redwood.ai/pr-2345

claire: LGTM aside from two tiny nits: 1) add a footnote about cached logs (we don't replicate logs cross-region by default), 2) show a short curl example for the regional endpoint that uses the env var pattern. i'll push a small patch for those gems.

miguel: pushed the footnote and the curl example you suggested. One outstanding ask: can someone from eng-runtime confirm the note I added about KV cache locality? i put "KV cache is region-local unless cross-region replication is enabled" — @alex-eng-runtime?

alex-eng-runtime: quick confirm: KV cache is per-cluster; for Dedicated and Private it's region-local unless customer requests replication. For Hosted we run a multi-region read-fallback for availability, so caches may be read across regions in failover scenarios. That matches the phrasing — you can add that sentence.

miguel: perfect — i've merged the wording updates and will merge the PR once CI finishes. thanks everyone! :tada:
